VERDICT: EXTEND C0021 | `_run_tool()` also returns `stderr="TIMEOUT"` for fix-evaluation test runs via `evaluate_fix(..., test_cmd=...)`. That path sets `tests_passed = (returncode == 0)`, so a timeout becomes `False` and the fix is marked `HARMFUL`. By contrast, timeouts in static-analysis runners currently collapse to empty diagnostics. The module therefore treats timeout as “tool found no issues” in one subsystem and “fix is harmful” in another. This inconsistency matters because SAFE/NEUTRAL verdicts feed `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` Stage 4, which sets `finding.verified = True`; timeout masking on pyright/ruff/bandit can incorrectly bless a fix after the same environment timed out on analysis elsewhere. Simplest downstream-safe fix: normalize timeout/not-found handling into explicit tool status and make verdict logic treat timed-out analyzers as unevaluable rather than zero-issue.

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.95
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not actually test fixes against a sandboxed copy of the codebase; it patches only the target file basename into a temp directory and then runs tools/tests against that isolated file or with `cwd=tmpdir`. Evidence: in `evaluate_fix`, `patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))` writes only one file; no package tree or sibling modules are copied. `run_pyright`, `run_ruff`, and `run_bandit` are then invoked on just `patched_path`. If `test_cmd` is provided, `_run_tool(test_cmd, cwd=tmpdir)` runs inside the tempdir without rewriting path arguments, so commands like the endocrine stage’s own `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...]` now execute from a directory that does not contain `bench/tests/`. This means imports, package-relative references, and actual project tests are not exercised against the patched code.
FOLLOW: Downstream, the advertised “sandbox-test proposed fixes” feature can return misleading SAFE/NEUTRAL verdicts for edits that break imports, cross-file interfaces, or package structure, because only the single patched file is analyzed in isolation. Worse, the immune pipeline consumes these verdicts in Stage 4 and marks findings `verified=True` when endocrine says SAFE/NEUTRAL. That flag closes bugs in later NK dedup/bug-closed gates, so a falsely safe isolated evaluation can prematurely close a still-broken bug across rounds. The current test execution path can also fail for environmental reasons unrelated to the fix because `cwd=tmpdir` disconnects relative test paths from the repository, making verdicts noisy and not representative of the real codebase.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — sandbox the relevant source tree, not just one file: create a tempdir, copy the project subtree containing the target file (at minimum the `bench/` package root) into it, apply the patch to the copied file at the same relative path, run tools on that copied path, and run `test_cmd` from the copied project root so relative test paths still resolve. This keeps “no source modification” while making fix evaluation exercise real imports/interfaces.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.34
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` can classify a harmful fix as `SAFE` when one tool’s issues increase and another’s decrease by a larger amount. Evidence: it computes `total_net = net_type_errors + net_ruff_errors + net_bandit_issues` and returns `HARMFUL` only if `total_net > 0`, `SAFE` if `total_net < 0`. Example from current fields: `net_type_errors = +3`, `net_ruff_errors = -5`, `net_bandit_issues = 0` yields `total_net = -2` and verdict `SAFE`, even though the fix introduced three new type errors. The docstring says `HARMFUL: new issues introduced`, which is stricter than the implementation.
FOLLOW: This crosses the immune interface directly. `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` Stage 4 marks findings verified when endocrine returns SAFE or NEUTRAL. A fix that introduces real new failures in one verifier can therefore still be marked verified if another tool count drops enough to offset it numerically. That can silently bless regressions and trigger bug-closed behavior in subsequent rounds, causing the system to stop pursuing a still-broken bug. Because this is silent misclassification rather than a crash, it is HIGH in PoC terms.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — treat any positive per-tool delta as harmful: if `net_type_errors > 0 or net_ruff_errors > 0 or net_bandit_issues > 0`, return `HARMFUL` immediately; otherwise keep the existing reduced/no-change logic for SAFE/NEUTRAL.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.84
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.48
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` measures only pyright, ruff, and bandit deltas, but `scan_health()` reports health from pyright, ruff, bandit, and mypy. Evidence: pre/post baselines in `evaluate_fix` call `_count_tool_issues(run_pyright|run_ruff|run_bandit, ...)`; there are no `pre_mypy_errors`, `new_mypy_errors`, or mypy contribution in `_compute_fix_verdict()`. This creates an interface mismatch inside the same module: a fix can worsen mypy-detected errors while still being classified SAFE/NEUTRAL.
FOLLOW: The endocrine layer is consumed as a mechanical health monitor and fix verifier. If health scan exposes mypy findings to the insect brain but fix evaluation ignores mypy regressions, the system can report “fix verified” even when one of its own enabled analyzers shows the patch is worse. That inconsistency feeds the immune pipeline’s verified flag and can close bugs on a false basis. It also misleads human reviewers because scan_health and evaluate_fix disagree on what counts as code health.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — include mypy in fix-evaluation baselines and deltas, parallel to pyright/ruff/bandit, and incorporate positive mypy regression into `HARMFUL`.
VERIFIED: TRUE
